findings.reason: the section should name `_search_code` as the code-search owner and either route `find_code` through `rerank_candidates` or state why the two code paths may return different orders.
findings.text: §9 ("`_search_code` and `_search_docs` rerank their top candidates through `rerank_candidates`") extends `_search_code` (with `_vector_search_code_chunks` at `imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:1531`) while leaving the second agent-facing code search, `find_code` at `imas_codex/graph/domain_queries.py:439` — registered for agents in the REPL registry at `imas_codex/llm/server.py:1586` — un-reranked, though it runs its own vector search over the same `code_chunk_embedding` index and returns candidates `ORDER BY score DESC`; the third ranked entry point, `_search_signals` at `imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:75` (tool at `imas_codex/llm/server.py:2385`), is likewise left out, though its different modality may be a deliberate exclusion. After §9 the same code query is answered by two owners (`_search_code` and `find_code`), only one of which reranks, so they will disagree on ordering

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one function, `rerank_candidates`, hides pool sizing, per-candidate state construction, the concurrency and wall-time bound, the cost total and the position-preserving failure merge behind a single call both tools make, over `decide_batch`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9 reranks one of two agent-facing code searches over the same `code_chunk_embedding` index and leaves the other, `find_code`, un-reranked, so the same code query will return differently-ordered results through the two paths.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §9 states it adds one module and one function, that the plan has one decision loop (the merge of the per-pipeline decision loops) and that the rerank adds no seat by reusing `discovery-relevance`, so it accounts for its added surface and the earlier seat finding is answered by removal.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §9 cites both call sites by file:line (`imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:683` and `:1429`), the existing seat (`discovery-relevance`, `imas_codex/settings.py:181`) and `score_composite`, and no rerank mechanism pre-exists (a grep for rerank finds only `sorted()` comments at `imas_codex/search/engines/hybrid_engine.py:87` and `imas_codex/search/search_strategy.py:454`), so `rerank_candidates` is not a rebuild of existing machinery.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `rerank_candidates` is not a bare forward to `decide_batch`; it adds query-plus-candidate state building, a pool larger than the returned window, and a failure path that returns the embedding order unchanged, none of which `decide_batch` (concurrency, budget, cost, None-on-failure) provides.
